solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Discover Devonian chap maybe, no artist

indicators.note: 'no artist' says the painter's abbreviation is absent, so those letters come out of the word

parts.note: West Country dialect word for a person, so a Devon man is an example

explanation.surface: Someone finds a man from Devon who is not a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: SPRAY is a West Country dialect word for a person; take RA out of it to leave SPY. 'Maybe' marks the Devonian as one example of such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy something is to catch sight of it, a common synonym for discovering it.

clue.text: Group of swimmers seeing second foolish flier heading off

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Icarus flew too near the sun and fell

explanation.surface: A shoal is spotted, then a reckless bird loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarus is the genus of the parrotfishes, so a biological group of fish.

clue.text: Church member Norm is greeting one before start of requiem

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

explanation.surface: A man called Norm welcomes people at a funeral mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Norm looks like a man's name; it is the word norm, meaning par.
explanation.definitionFit: A parishioner belongs to a parish, the local community of a church.

clue.text: Happened to be joined to a husband in marriage

parts.note: as in 'what has been', what has happened

explanation.surface: Someone just happened to end up wed to a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Beenah is a form of marriage, found in Sri Lanka, where the husband goes to live with the wife's family.

clue.text: Rodents possibly snarl at first sign of dog

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements of the letters that follow
the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Rats snarl when they first see a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Land rats are rats living on land, as against ship's rats or water rats, so rodents.

clue.text: Dull Greek character, unruly adolescent once

parts.note: a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth known for rowdiness

explanation.surface: A boring Greek and a 1950s tearaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Teds were young men of 1950s Britain in Edwardian-style clothes, with a rowdy reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A muted colour or sound is subdued, toned down and so dull.

clue.text: Cloth to lose distinct shape, being worn

parts.note: something that melts loses its form

explanation.surface: A fabric that goes out of shape once someone wears it.
explanation.definitionFit: Melton is a heavy woollen cloth with a felted finish, used for overcoats.

clue.text: The writer squeezed by lass becomes injured

indicators.note: something squeezed by another is pressed inside it

parts.note: the writer is the setter, me

explanation.surface: The author, hugged too hard by a girl, gets hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Maimed means badly wounded, crippled by an injury.

clue.text: Old body organ's all in, done for, without energy

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the letters go around
something done for is wrecked, so the preceding letters are broken up

explanation.surface: An exhausted, finished patient lacking any energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without energy' reads as 'lacking energy', but without means outside: the rearranged letters surround E.
explanation.definitionFit: Lienal means relating to the spleen, from Latin lien; the organ's name is old, hence 'old body organ's'.

clue.text: Some fungal structures are excellent, growing up in grass

indicators.note: one part placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to grass is to inform on, to tell

indicators.note: in a down clue, growing up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A1, excellent, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: Mushrooms thriving in a lawn are a fine sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is British slang for informing to the police, which is to tell on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Telia are spore-bearing bodies of rust fungi; telial describes them, as some fungal structures are.

clue.text: Information introducing commercial making one old freshly despondent

explanation.surface: A news item leads into an advert that makes an old man newly gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One old' signals an archaic word: this is Spenser's.
explanation.definitionFit: New-sad is a Spenserian compound meaning newly sad, made sorrowful afresh.

clue.text: Barrel or cask, a superior gift

parts.note: a cade is a barrel or cask, so both words describe the one word

explanation.surface: A barrel of something good offered as a fine present.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' usage of British speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadeau is the French word for a present, used in English for a gift or token.

clue.text: Each expert collects prize (6, two words)

indicators.note: one who collects something holds it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: pie in the sense of a desirable reward or share of the spoils

explanation.surface: Every specialist picks up an award.
explanation.walkthrough: Prize as pie is the stretch here: pie as a reward or share of the spoils. 'Collects' means the expert's word wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'A piece' means for each one, as in 'a pound a piece', the same as each.

clue.text: Holiday site is in Brittany with endless laughing in the fields

indicators.note: with no end, the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A campsite in Brittany full of constant laughter out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Brittany is in France, so 'is' there is French est.
explanation.definitionFit: Campestrian means of or growing in fields, from Latin campus, a field.

clue.text: Fellow in a ceremony makes one glance

indicators.note: a fellow placed in a ceremony is enclosed by that word

explanation.surface: A man at a ceremony catches someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance' is not a look here: in mineralogy it is a lustrous ore, and silver glance is another name for this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentite is silver sulphide, a metallic ore known as silver glance, so it is one glance among several.

clue.text: Some crooked nutcase going round, not straight

indicators.note: to go round is to turn about, so the letters run backwards
'some' means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: letters spanning the two words, read backwards

explanation.surface: A twisted lunatic going round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across crookED NUtcase and are read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Undé is a heraldic term for a wavy line or edge, so not straight.

clue.text: Notes skimpy attire on modern miss

parts.note: Ms, the modern title for a woman

explanation.surface: A comment on a young woman's revealing outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth two crotchets, a half note in American terms.

clue.text: American protection coming to you and me

parts.note: ward in the sense of guard or protection

explanation.surface: American security forces arriving at our door.
explanation.definitionFit: Usward is an old adverb meaning towards us, in our direction.

clue.text: Dealing with old age, with groin etc in trouble

indicators.note: things in trouble are in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Elderly care involving a groin injury and other ailments.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerontic means relating to old age, from Greek geron, an old man.

clue.text: Music's ultimate composer took the initiative and suddenly turned up

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: to lead is to take the initiative

explanation.surface: A composer took charge of the music's finale and suddenly appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like 'arrived', but it is literal: a climbing turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandelle is an abrupt climbing turn by an aircraft; to chandelle is to make one, turning and rising suddenly.

clue.text: Extinct mammals absent, in a place below the earth

indicators.note: being in a place means being enclosed by it

explanation.surface: Long-dead beasts missing, buried in an underground spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the classical name for the underworld, and for its ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinotheres were huge elephant-like animals with down-curving tusks, long since died out.

clue.text: Awful snag, hollowed-out wood being used for bits of timber

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are put in a new order
hollowed out means emptied of its inside, keeping only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A carpenter hits a nasty knot in hollow wood used for timber pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwangs are short timber struts or noggings set between joists or studs, mainly a Scots and New Zealand word.

clue.text: Intellectual observation — East will make advance

indicators.note: to advance is to move forward, so a letter shifts to an earlier place inside the word

explanation.surface: A remark that the East will push forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The E at the end of NOTICE moves up two places to give NOETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Noetic means of the intellect or mind, from Greek noesis, thinking.

clue.text: Old Irish sage gives a word of welcome, turning up to entertain maiden

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom upwards
to entertain a guest is to take them in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: M for maiden, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An old Irish wise man greets someone and turns up to host a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: An ollamh was a master poet or learned scholar of the highest rank in old Ireland.

clue.text: Jock's collecting fine stuff to display on street

explanation.surface: A Scotsman gathers fine goods to show off in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is the stock nickname for a Scot, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairst is Scots for harvest, the season of gathering in the crops.

clue.text: Swindler ruining soccer

indicators.note: ruining means wrecking, so the next word's letters are broken and remade

explanation.surface: A cheat spoiling the football.
explanation.definitionFit: Escroc is a French-derived word for a swindler or con man.

clue.text: In Glasgow, must not mother and girl hide name?

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so a letter goes within

explanation.surface: A Glasgow mother tells her daughter they must not conceal their name.
explanation.walkthrough: Una and Ena are equally good girls' names here; only the crossing letters settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maunna is Scots for must not, so it is what a Glaswegian would say.

clue.text: Very good old-fashioned nonsense — thanks!

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the old ways as rubbish, then says thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash looks like a pause in speech; it only separates the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boshta is dated Australian slang for excellent, so an old-fashioned word for very good.

clue.text: Startling sounds associated with drug and drink

parts.note: boo! is said to startle someone

explanation.surface: Shock noises linked to narcotics and alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Boose is an old spelling of booze, so alcoholic drink or to drink heavily.

clue.text: Sick girl rolling over? It's the pasta

indicators.note: something rolling over turns upside down, so the words run back to front

explanation.surface: An ill girl tossing in bed blames the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Anelli are small ring-shaped pasta pieces, used mostly in soups.

clue.text: Individual may catch cold at any time

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so one letter is taken inside

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Anybody can come down with a cold whenever.
explanation.definitionFit: 'If once' means if ever, so once can mean at any time.

clue.text: Vehicle rushed round in a shower

indicators.note: one part placed in another sits inside it
turned round means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A car sped around during a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aérotrain was an experimental French hovercraft train, a vehicle running on an air cushion along a track.

clue.text: Singing fisherman gets very dirty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Peter ..., the fisherman in Britten's opera
second meaning: a verb from grime, to soil thoroughly

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fisherman getting filthy; the title role of Britten's opera Peter Grimes is a sung fisherman.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is soot or dirt ground in, and as a verb to grime something is to make it filthy.

clue.text: Like some natives abused in USA, retaining nothing

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece is held inside the other
abused means mistreated and knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Indigenous Americans mistreated in the US and left with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Siouan describes the language family of the Sioux and related peoples, so it fits some Native Americans.

clue.text: Son has a box, having lost special bag

indicators.note: to have lost something is to be without it, so that letter goes

explanation.surface: A boy owns a container but has mislaid a particular bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed bag or packet, as of sugar or shampoo.

clue.text: Prince denied king's collection

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a rana is a Rajput prince in India

explanation.surface: A prince is refused the king's set of treasures.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ana is a collection of someone's sayings or anecdotes, the noun behind the suffix in Victoriana.
